edits.target: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
edits.content: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For common-noun definition clues, give the requested category term rather than examples; use the canonical headword form (normally singular for a generic count noun) and include a required article rather than mechanically copying the plural number of examples in the clue or context. When asked what something was nicknamed, give the nickname phrase itself; do not append a generic entity label (such as “Party”) just because the referent belongs to that category. For people, use the full conventional identity when no name component is supplied; when a clue supplies a name component and asks who or for completion, give only the missing component. Preserve integral distinguishing parts of conventional names, such as a regnal numeral, while omitting optional middle initials, generational suffixes, and honorifics. Avoid explanations and alternatives.

edits.target: - Identify the specific entity, attribute, or relation requested before answering. Treat clue-like statements or fragments as implicit questions and return the missing value, not a judgment about whether the statement is true. Give the named referent rather than a related person, description, or broad topic; use a true/false answer only when explicitly requested.

When a fragment consists of a date and place, use the context to identify the person or entity directly associated with those anchors and return that referent, not an event paraphrase such as “X’s birth,” unless the event itself is requested. Give the named referent rather than a related person, description, or broad topic; use a true/false answer only when explicitly requested.
